sentences.text:
This Appeal is filed by the Appellant aggrieved by the Award passed in ECA.No.85/2014, on the file of the II Addl. Senior Civil Judge, Shivamogga, dated 08.11.2016, whereby the Tribunal has granted meager compensation amount of Rs.4,70,525/-.
NC: 2023:KHC:41252 2.

entities.text: II Addl. Senior Civil Judge, Shivamogga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.48,00,000/- on account of the injuries suffered by the claimant.
It is the case of the claimant that accident took place on 22.12.2012 and the son of the petitioner No.1 died.

It is a case of the appellant herein that he is Sri Sridhar R vs Smt Jnanamma on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72264647/
2 running a travel agency and deceased was working with him from the past one year and they used to pay salary of Rs.15,000/- and in addition to this, he used to get Rs.50 to 100/- as bata charges.

entities.text: Sri Sridhar R vs Smt Jnanamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As accident had taken place during the course of his employment, the employer as well as Insurance Company are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

It is the case of the appellant herein before the Tribunal that the deceased was working with him from the last 2 to 3 months as a temporary driver and was getting an amount of Rs.3,500/- and the bata is paid by the customer, but not by him.

The appellant's defence was that there is no employer and employee relationship between the parties and as such the application itself is not maintainable.
NC: 2023:KHC:41252 3.
It is the stand of the Insurance Company that the deceased did have license to drive a Light Motor Vehicle/ non transport vehicle.
But he was driving a transport vehicle as such the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

The Court below on the issue of the employer and employee relationship on the admission made by the owner of the vehicle that he has been working with him from the last 2 to 3 months and why he was driving the vehicle belonging to the owner of the vehicle the accident had taken place has held that there is employee and employer relationship.

When it comes to the liability of the Insurance Company, the Court has held that as the driver was not having a driving license to drive a non-transport vehicle, the Insurance Company was absolved from the liability and held that owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
4.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/ owner of the vehicle submits that there is no employer and employee relationship and this aspect was not properly NC: 2023:KHC:41252 appreciated by the Court below.

It is submitted that when a petition is filed under Section 2 of the Employees Compensation Act, the burden lies on the petitioner to prove that there is employer and employee relationship between the parties.
Apart from that it is submitted that the Court below went wrong in absolving the Insurance Company from the liability.
It is submitted that this case is squarely covered by the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court MUKUND DEWANGAN -V- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED1,.

entities.text: MUKUND DEWANGAN -V- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that the Tribunal without appreciating any of the evidence on record and the legal position has granted compensation by exonerating the Insurance Company from the liability.

5. Learned counsel for the claimant submit that the Court below had rightly considered the relationship between the parties i.e., employer-employee relationship and has rightly granted the compensation.
He further submits that no grounds are made out for interfering with the well considered order passed by the Court below.
Though notice is served on the Insurance Company, there is no representation on their behalf.
7. Heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.

As far as the employer and employee relationship is concerned, this Court is not able to appreciate any of the submission made by the learned counsel for the appellant that there is no employee and employer relationship.
There is a clear admission on the part of the appellant himself that the deceased was working from the last 2 to 3 months and he has been paying the salary.

In that case, no other Sri Sridhar R vs Smt Jnanamma on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72264647/
3 material is required from the employee to substantiate his case that there is a relationship between employer and employee.

entities.text: Sri Sridhar R vs Smt Jnanamma on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court below had rightly considered this aspect and held that there is a relationship of employer and employee.

8. When it comes to the liability of the Insurance Company, the deceased was having a license to drive a Light Motor Vehicle/non transport vehicle, but he was NC: 2023:KHC:41252 driving a light motor transport vehicle and that cannot be a ground for the Court below to exempt the Insurance Company.
9. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MUKUND DEWANGAN -V- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED2, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.

entities.text: MUKUND DEWANGAN -V- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appeal of the owner is partly allowed.
By holding that there is an employee and employer relationship between the deceased and the appellant.
The Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Accordingly, appeal is partly allowed.
i) The amount in deposit shall be forthwith transmitted to the Tribunal.
The owner of the vehicle is at liberty to withdraw the amount in deposit and the Insurance Company shall deposit the amount within a period of 8 weeks.
ii) The respondent - Insurance  Company shall deposit the amount  (2017) 14 SCC 663  NC: 2023:KHC:41252 within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment.

On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing any security.
iii) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
iv) No costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

SD/-
